st: Put the horse meat, lamb, 1 whole onion, bay leaves and peppercorns in a large pot with [[12 cups]] water. Bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Reduce to a low simmer and cook for 2 hours, skimming now and then, until the meat is tender.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, 2 eggs, [[1 tsp]] salt and about [[0.5 cup]] warm water into a firm dough. Knead 5 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Lift the meat out of the pot, strain the broth, and keep both warm. Cut the meat off the bones into bite-size pieces.
Simmer the sliced onions in [[1 cup]] of the broth with [[0.5 tsp]] salt for 10 minutes until soft.
Roll the dough thin and cut into 3-inch squares or diamonds.
Bring the broth back to a boil with [[1 tsp]] salt and cook the noodle squares in batches for 5 minutes until tender.
Pile the noodles on a large platter, top with the meat and onions, and sprinkle with herbs.
Serve with cups of hot broth on the side.
Stir [[2.25 tsp]] yeast and [[2 tbsp]] sugar into [[1 cup]] warm milk and wait 5 minutes until foamy.
Add the eggs, [[3 tbsp]] melted butter and [[1 tsp]] salt and whisk.
Mix in [[3.5 cups]] flour to make a soft dough, then knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Roll the dough about 0.5 inch thick and cut into 2-inch squares or diamonds.
Rest the pieces for 10 minutes under a towel.
Heat [[4 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the dough pieces in batches for 2 to 3 minutes, turning, until puffed and golden brown all over.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with tea, jam or honey.

ing: rib meat with bones; or use beef or lamb ribs
st: Cut the meat into strips about 1 inch thick and chop the fat into small pieces. Remove large bones.
Mix the meat and fat with [[6 cloves]] garlic, [[1 tbsp]] cumin, [[1 tbsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours so the flavors absorb.
Rinse the casings well and tie one end of each with kitchen string.
Stuff the meat mixture loosely into each casing and tie the open end, leaving a little room for expansion.
Bring [[12 cups]] water with the bay leaves to a gentle simmer in a big pot. Do not let it boil hard.
Add the sausages and poach for 2.5 hours until the meat reaches at least 160°F (71°C) and is tender.
Let cool in the liquid for 30 minutes and slice into rounds. Serve warm or cold with bread and pickles.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a heavy skillet or pot over medium-high heat.
Fry the lamb cubes for 8 minutes until browned all over.
Add the liver and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until no pink remains.
Add the onions and cook for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the potatoes, [[1.5 tsp]] salt, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and [[0.5 cup]] water.
Cover and cook on medium-low for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potatoes are tender and the lamb is cooked through.
Stir in [[2 cloves]] garlic and cook 1 minute. Taste for salt.
Sprinkle with [[0.25 cup]] dill and serve hot with bread.
Rinse the rice in several changes of cold water until clear, then soak in warm salted water for 30 minutes.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] oil in a heavy pot over high heat until shimmering. Brown the lamb for 8 minutes.
Add the onions and cook for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the carrots and cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until they soften slightly. Add [[1 tbsp]] cumin, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Pour in [[1 cup]] boiling water, cover, and simmer on low for 30 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Drain the rice and spread it evenly over the meat without stirring. Push the garlic head into the center.
Pour [[3 cups]] boiling water gently on the rice, until covered by 1 inch. Cook uncovered on high until the water is almost gone.
Poke a few holes, cover tightly, and cook on lowest heat for 20 minutes until the rice is tender.
Rest 10 minutes, then mix gently and serve with the garlic and meat on top.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and about [[1 cup]] warm water into a stiff dough. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and rest, covered, for 30 minutes.
Mix the lamb, onions, pumpkin, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and [[0.5 tsp]] cumin for the filling.
Roll out the dough very thin and cut it into 4-inch squares.
Place about [[2 tbsp]] filling in the center of each square.
Bring the corners up and pinch the edges together to form a closed parcel with a sealed top.
Oil a steamer rack. Arrange the manti with space between them.
Steam over boiling water for 45 minutes. The lamb should reach 160°F (71°C).
Serve hot, drizzled with [[3 tbsp]] melted butter, with sour cream or broth on the side.

ing: spaghetti or udon will also work
st: Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large heavy pot over high heat and brown the beef for 6 minutes.
Add the onion and carrots and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste and [[1 tsp]] cumin for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and bell peppers and cook 5 minutes.
Pour in [[3 cups]] water, add [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the beef is tender.
Boil the noodles in a separate pot of salted water per package directions, usually 4 to 6 minutes, and drain.
Taste the sauce and adjust the seasoning.
Divide the noodles among bowls and ladle the beef and vegetables over the top. Sprinkle with [[0.25 cup]] cilantro.
Rinse the lamb and put it in a large pot with [[10 cups]] cold water.
Bring slowly to a boil, then skim off all the foam for the first 10 minutes to keep the broth clear.
Add the whole onions, bay leaves, peppercorns and [[2 tsp]] salt.
Cover and simmer very gently for 1.5 hours until the lamb is tender. Do not let it boil hard.
Add the carrots and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook 20 more minutes until all are tender.
Taste the broth and add salt if needed.
Ladle into bowls with a piece of lamb and vegetables in each, then sprinkle with fresh herbs.
Whisk [[3 cups]] flour, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] baking powder in a bowl.
Stir in [[1 cup]] warm milk and [[2 tbsp]] melted butter to make a soft dough.
Knead for 5 minutes until smooth, then cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 balls.
Roll each ball out into a thin round about 7 inches wide.
Pour [[1 cup]] oil into a wide skillet, to a depth of about 0.5 inch, and heat over medium-high.
Fry each flatbread for 1 to 2 minutes per side until puffed with golden spots.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with tea, jam or soup.
